text:
Nick Robertson has seven goals and zero assists in 18 games, which is a very specific kind of season. He's doing it on the Penguins' third line at about 13 minutes a night, and The Hockey News thinks he's about to get another shot in the top six, a spot it argues he never should have left.

The chances are real. He has 4.29 expected goals (the quality of his chances), among the better rates for a depth forward, and the Penguins take 61% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, ten points better than without him. That's why he's one of our Sleepers tonight in San Jose. The finishing is the part that won't last: 21% shooting against 13% last season, and our numbers flag him as due to cool. The assists are the strange part. Zero in 18 games for a forward on a line that's driving play is partly bad luck and partly who he is, more finisher than passer. If he does move up beside better players, our range still has him finishing around 23 goals.
